chunks: And Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from a group of our companions, among them Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan (in his hadith), who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): May I ask you? He said: Ask your Imam. I said: Who do you mean? For I do not know any Imam other than you. He said: It is Ali, my son, whom I have given my kunya (agnomen). I said: My master, save me from the Fire, for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, you are the Qaim (the one standing/active) in this matter! He said: Was I not the Qaim? Then he said: O Hasan, there is no Imam who is the Qaim in a community except that he is their Qaim. And when they pass away from them, the one who succeeds them is the Qaim. The Hujjah (Divine Proof) until he becomes concealed from them, so all of us are Qaim. So direct all that you were treating me with to my son Ali. (By Allah) By Allah, it was not I who did that to him, but Allah did that to him.

key_terms.حجة: Hujjah (Divine Proof, a title for the Imam)
key_terms.قائم: Qaim (the active, recognized Imam or one standing in authority)
key_terms.كنية: Kunya (agnomen, a nickname derived from one's child's name)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Qaim after Imam Musa al-Kadhim and what is the meaning of the Imam being 'Qaim'?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* elucidates the dynamic nature of the 'Qaim' (the active, presiding Imam) within the lineage of the Twelve Imams, establishing that each Imam is the 'Qaim' of his era until his death or concealment. Imam Musa al-Kadhim explicitly designates his son Ali al-Rida as the successor, reinforcing the doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation) while clarifying that the continuity of Imamate is divinely ordained rather than merely a human administrative act. This narrative serves as a crucial bridge in Shia eschatology, linking the visible Imamate of the early Imams to the eventual occultation of the final Hujjah.
